sharp.runtime: glibc optional dependencies via dedicated NODE_PATH

sandboxPrivilegeQualification.observed: Stock job initialization needs chroot/setgroups/setgid/setuid. Python additionally chowns a 0600 bootstrap before launching its root interpreter; root without DAC bypass cannot read that foreign-owned file. Node works with three caps; root-owned Node extraction plus a Python preopened-stdin adapter worked with four. This is not unmodified-stock feasibility.
sandboxPrivilegeQualification.policy: Root TCB includes bounded provisioning/sshd supervision and a trusted sandbox broker/launcher. Broker operative caps are limited to CHOWN,SETUID,SETGID,SYS_CHROOT. Nonroot services/jobs have zero inheritable/permitted/effective/ambient caps; job supplementary groups empty, no-new-privileges, seccomp and private root. Reserve GID1000 exclusively for pooled jobs and keep service/dev identities outside their UID pool. Broker can access root secrets; no root-broker isolation from keys is claimed. Disable preload, runtime package installation and dependency mutation/refresh inside the broker, not merely a proxy. Root-consumed bootstrap must never be job-writable; no UID reuse until all job descendants are reaped. The temporary ownership-handoff prototype needs production hardening and independent policy review.

spike.scope: One bounded isolated feasibility spike with candidate/instrumentation iterations; not TDD, full-image integration or production security qualification.

node.rootPositiveControl: All three synthetic canaries readable outside job chroot.

python.adaptation: Root-owned extraction, scratch adapter validated path/type/owner/mode/parent, temporarily chowned bootstrap to root to preopen, restored job ownership, then fed existing FD as stdin to stock Python; FD3 user-code pipe preserved. No DAC bypass cap.

lowPortControl.effect: All nonroot identities can bind low ports in this network namespace; not a per-role capability.

negativeAndDiagnosticControls: Three-cap Node succeeds; Python bootstrap chown rejected with operation-not-permitted.
Four-cap stock startup hit Node exec permission denial; root-owned tar extraction resolved it.
Node identity instrumentation hit seccomp operation-not-permitted; use allowed getuid and external kernel proc status instead.
Reopening an inherited foreign-owned 0600 file via /proc/self/fd was denied; consuming the already-open FD via stdin succeeded.
Scratch adapter ownership was normalized to root/mode0700 before execution.
